Nope.

Since space is constantly expanding, and since there is only a set amount of energy within the universe, once space grows large enough and once time progresses, matter and energy will become so dispersed throughout the universe that no meaningful work (in the physics sense) can be performed by objects interacting with one another (i.e. maximum entropy) and causing temperatures to approach absolute zero uniformly throughout the universe. This is what is refer to as heat death of the universe.

For many years there were several competing hypothesis about the ultimate behavior of the universe. The Big Crunch was another hypothesis that asserted that at some point, due to gravity, the expansion of the universe (due to the big bang) would be halted and all matter would eventually collapse together into a singularity. This behavior would lead to and endless cyclical universe of bangs and crunches. Unfortunately physics does not work this way due to thermodynamics.

Fortunately heat death is some trillions of years into the future so it's not a real serious problem. We'll be lucky if our species can survive the next century, let alone long enough to worry about our own sun expanding and swallowing Earth in a storm of fiery death.
